title: Raw values still visible on a stem-and-leaf diagram
source: S1 Ch1 theory S1-1.5 Quick check 1 (14 ungrouped discrete readings, all 14 still visible)
stem: A stem-and-leaf diagram is drawn for {n|int} ungrouped discrete readings. How many of those raw readings can still be read from the diagram?

steps.name: form
steps.text_tex: A stem-and-leaf diagram keeps every raw value.
steps.note: Use the fact that raw values remain visible.

steps.name: E
steps.text_tex: All \({n|int}\) readings can still be read.

contexts.stem: A coach records {n|int} ungrouped sprint times and displays them in a stem-and-leaf diagram. How many of the original times can still be read from the diagram?
{n|int} ungrouped test scores are shown in a stem-and-leaf diagram. How many of those raw scores remain visible?

title: Individual recordings hidden by a histogram
source: S1 Ch1 theory S1-1.5 Quick check 2 (grouped continuous data in a histogram, 0 raw values readable exactly)
stem: A histogram is drawn from {n|int} grouped continuous observations. How many of the original individual recordings can be read exactly from the histogram?

steps.name: form
steps.text_tex: Grouping for a histogram hides the individual recordings.
steps.note: Use the fact that a histogram does not show raw values.

steps.name: E
steps.text_tex: The number that can be read exactly is \(0\).

contexts.stem: The masses of {n|int} parcels are grouped and displayed in a histogram. How many of the original individual masses can be read exactly from the histogram?
A histogram is drawn for the grouped heights of {n|int} trees. How many of the original individual heights can be read exactly from the histogram?

title: How many listed representations suit large grouped continuous data
source: S1 Ch1 theory S1-1.5 Quick check 3 (2 of 4 representations appropriate)
stem: A large set of grouped continuous measurements is to be displayed. A list of {total|int} representations is considered: a histogram and a cumulative frequency graph (appropriate), and a stem-and-leaf diagram and a pie chart (not appropriate). How many of the representations in the list are appropriate for this type and quantity of data?

steps.name: form
steps.text_tex: A histogram and a cumulative frequency graph are appropriate; a stem-and-leaf diagram and a pie chart are not.

steps.name: E
steps.text_tex: The number of appropriate representations is \({E|int}\).

contexts.stem: For a large set of grouped continuous measurements, {m|int} representations in a list of {total|int} are appropriate (a histogram and a cumulative frequency graph) and the other {k|int} are not (a stem-and-leaf diagram and a pie chart). How many of the representations in the list are appropriate?

An audience is to be shown a large set of grouped continuous data. Of the {total|int} representations considered, only a histogram and a cumulative frequency graph are appropriate. How many of those representations are appropriate?
